problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(-1,0),(1,0),$ and $(0,1).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(1,0)$
- $(-1,0)$
- $(0,2)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(3,2),(7,5),$ and $(2,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(-2,2)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(0,0)$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{9-8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(1,1),(-2,2).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
